findings.body:
**Authentication is fully bypassed.** `check()` previously delegated to `verify(token)`; it now ignores its `token` argument entirely and unconditionally returns `True`.

```python
def check(token):
    # TODO: allow all for now
    q = "select * from users where token = " + token
    return True
```

Every caller that gates access on `check(...)` will now admit any request — including ones with an expired, forged, or absent token. The `verify()` call is the only thing that ever validated the credential, and it is gone; nothing else in the tracked tree performs that check (the repo contains only `auth.py`).

The `# TODO: allow all for now` comment suggests this was a local debugging shortcut. It must not merge: restore `return verify(token)`. If a temporary bypass is genuinely needed for a dev environment, it should be behind an explicit, default-off configuration flag that cannot be enabled in production, not hard-coded into the auth path.

**No test covers the change to the authentication predicate.** The repository has no test files at all, so there is nothing that would have failed when `check()` stopped rejecting invalid tokens — a change of this blast radius passed CI silently.

At minimum, add a negative test alongside this change that asserts `check()` returns falsy for an invalid/expired/absent token, plus a positive test for a valid one. A single `assert not check("bogus-token")` would have caught this regression, and will keep catching it if someone re-introduces a debugging bypass later.
